input: Research Carvana (carvana.com) for a hedge fund

risks.claim: Unit growth can mask weaker unit economics: for Q3 ended 2026-09-30, GAAP gross profit per unit fell $365 YoY to $6,997 and adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 10.0% from 11.3%, despite 39% unit growth. Continued compression could undermine earnings growth.

Funding dependency: the Q3 filing reports dependence on revolving financing and receivable sales; as of 2026-09-30 its $7.503bn broad liquidity measure included uncommitted additional debt capacity. Loss of financing access would make that headline materially less protective than cash.

Governance risk: as described in the 2026-09-30 filing, qualifying Garcia-party Class B shares generally carry ten votes each, subject to the ownership threshold. Economic ownership percentages therefore do not capture voting influence.

Forecast visibility will decrease: management announced on 2026-10-28 that quarterly and annual outlooks will cease beginning with the Q4 2026 call. Investors will have less company-provided near-term benchmarking even as gross profit per unit is declining.

output.company: Carvana Co. (NYSE: CVNA); research as of 2026-11-10

catalysts.claim: Q4/FY2026 earnings are the next major catalyst: Investing.com lists 2027-02-25, but the company has not confirmed that date in the opened events calendar as of 2026-11-10. Treat the date as provisional, not a scheduled company event.

At the Q4 2026 earnings call, management plans to stop providing quarterly and annual financial outlooks; in 2027 it will shift primary reporting toward GAAP metrics. This changes the framework for estimating growth and margins; announced 2026-10-28, exact call date unconfirmed.

event_driven.claim: Completed liability-management event: on 2026-08-14 Carvana borrowed $1.660bn under a Term Loan B and used proceeds plus cash to redeem all $1.660bn of its 9% secured notes due 2030. Q3 2026 included a $53m debt-extinguishment loss; this was a debt redemption, not an equity buyback.

Capital-structure comparability: the five-for-one forward split was effected 2026-05-08. The Q3 2026 filing retroactively adjusts share and per-share figures for all presented periods; unadjusted older ownership counts are not comparable.

output.research_view: As of 2026-11-10, the key question is whether rapid unit growth can offset declining profit per vehicle: Q3 delivered record volume and EBITDA, but lower GPU and EBITDA margin ([Q3 shareholder letter](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000066/ex99_1q32026.htm)). Liquidity and the completed refinancing reduce immediate financing pressure, while the planned withdrawal of short-term guidance raises the importance of independently tracking inventory, conversion and loan-sale economics ([Q3 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000067/cvna-20260930.htm); [shareholder letter](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000066/ex99_1q32026.htm)).

credit_signals.claim: As of 2026-09-30, total debt excluding finance leases was $5.161bn, including $2.269bn secured notes, $1.660bn Term Loan B, $1.125bn asset-based financing and $107m unsecured notes; $302m was current.

As of 2026-09-30, cash and equivalents were $3.049bn and borrowing availability against eligible collateral was $2.071bn, giving $5.120bn committed liquidity resources. The broader $7.503bn liquidity figure also includes debt-incurrence baskets and unpledged securitization interests; it is not all cash or committed funding.

The Term Loan B entered 2026-08-14 matures in 2033 and bears Term SOFR plus 225 basis points; its effective interest rate was approximately 6.1% as of 2026-09-30. It extends the refinanced 2030 maturity but introduces floating-rate exposure.

Carvana reported compliance with all debt covenants as of 2026-09-30. During Q3 it increased Ally’s finance-receivable purchase commitment to up to $8bn through July 2027 and extended a short-term revolver through August 2027.

alternative_signals.claim: Local hiring signal, announced 2026-10-06: Carvana had begun hiring for IRC capabilities at ADESA Orlando and expected approximately 100 inspection, reconditioning and fulfillment jobs over time. This is a site-specific hiring plan, not evidence of a company-wide workforce increase.

As reported 2026-10-28 for Q3, two more ADESA sites gained retail production capabilities, bringing integrated sites to 21. Three full buildouts were under construction and expected to begin production during 2027; the latest letter does not commit all three to the next six months.

Capacity as reported 2026-10-28: approximately 1.5m retail units of fully built-out annual capacity, with real estate supporting 3m annual units. These are management capacity estimates, not sales guidance or independent channel checks.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Latest reported quarter: Q3 ended 2026-09-30. Retail units were 217,385 (+39% YoY), revenue $8.040bn (+42%), net income $483m, adjusted EBITDA $800m and diluted Class A EPS $0.39; reported 2026-10-28.

Against company guidance: the 2026-07-29 outlook called for Q3 retail units above Q2 and FY2026 adjusted EBITDA of $2.7bn–$3.0bn. Q2 units were 197,325; Q3 units of 217,385 satisfied the directional unit outlook. No numeric Q3 EPS or EBITDA target was verified.

Against consensus at the 2026-10-28 release: reported EPS of $0.39 missed the $0.44 analyst estimate by $0.05; revenue of $8.04bn exceeded the $7.67bn consensus. These are the consensus figures reported by Investing.com, not company guidance.

Current guidance as of 2026-10-28: Q4 retail units should increase sequentially and FY2026 adjusted EBITDA should land at the higher end of the previously communicated $2.7bn–$3.0bn range, conditional on a stable environment. No FY2027 annual financial guidance was verified.

insider_and_ownership.claim: CEO Ernest Garcia III’s Form 4 filed 2026-11-03 reports 7,072 shares withheld for taxes on 2026-11-01 at $68.29 and 4,702,660 direct shares afterward. This was tax withholding on vesting, not an open-market sale.
Thomas Taira sold 5,597 Class A shares at $65 on 2026-10-12, leaving 357,442 direct shares. His Form 4 filed 2026-10-13 says the sale was under a Rule 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-06-15.

Ernest Garcia II’s 13D/A filed 2026-11-03 reports 212,211,585 Class-A-equivalent beneficial shares, or 22.7%. On 2026-10-30 his SPE entered physically settled covered calls over 10m shares at $90, exercisable only 2027-11-19, outside the six-month catalyst window; this was not a completed underlying-share sale.

Secondary-source ownership check: TIKR’s November report on holdings as of 2026-06-30 identifies Electron Capital and GoldenTree as new holders and Durable Capital and Lone Pine as increasing stakes by at least one-fifth. Its comparison adjusts for the May split; these are stale Q2 positions, not verified current holdings.
